stage_a.note: He smiles warmly while holding the bananas and maintains a highly upbeat and engaging tone.
He uses energetic gestures and a lively voice when asking who wants to join him.
He tells a relatable story about brown bananas in a friendly, conversational and approachable manner.

venture.description: Silicone caps with interchangeable magnetic hats designed to slow down the ripening of bananas by inhibiting ethylene gas absorption at the crown.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 delivers the prepared presentation, explaining the problem of banana ripening and introducing the magnetic silicone cap solution.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if the device works by being placed through the top of the bananas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that the gas is still emitted but the device slows its spread to other bananas.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how long the device extends the freshness of the bananas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they make no specific claims but estimates it extends freshness by eight to twelve days.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 acknowledges that extending freshness by that amount of time is a valuable benefit.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if extending freshness is the reason grocery stores put green plastic wrap around banana stems.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that the grocery store practice uses the exact same methodology to slow ripening.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 expresses appreciation for learning a new fact about grocery store practices.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the retail price of the product and its manufacturing cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they sell a two-pack for twelve ninety-nine and the average cost is one ninety-five.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 suggests that selling just the silicone sock without the magnet would be significantly cheaper to produce.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 concedes that producing just the silicone sock would indeed be cheaper.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks why the founder did not just put a smiley face on the sock instead of the hat.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that consumers would not want to look at a plain sock on their bananas.

turns.speaker: UNKNOWN
turns.summary: The panel shares a laugh at the founder's response about not wanting to look at a sock.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what inspired the founder to come up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks for the origin of the product's name.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he got the idea in 2016 while trying to keep bananas fresh using duct tape and foil.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what the founder does for a living.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that he works as a wealth manager for a large investment bank.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 and the panel laugh at the contrast between the founder's profession and his product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 continues his story, explaining he learned to work remotely in 2020 and assembled the first units at home.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what has happened with the business since the initial assembly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that they achieved four hundred eighty-three thousand dollars in sales for the full year 2021.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 and S4 express strong positive surprise and excitement at the impressive sales figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokingly asks the panel if they are taking him seriously now after hearing the sales numbers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what the sales projections are for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 projects six hundred thousand in sales for the year, with a profit of two hundred forty thousand.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 expresses being impressed by the projected sales and profit margins.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks for the breakdown of sales between retail and direct-to-consumer channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that sixty percent of sales are direct-to-consumer and forty percent are wholesale.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what type of retail locations are carrying the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that most wholesale goes through one large online gift retailer, alongside a few mini novelty shops.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if the founder has tried reaching out to major grocery chains to gauge their interest.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says he has reached out extensively through calls and emails since it is a brand new product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 states he will not invest because the business is not a good fit for him, and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 praises the founder for successfully turning what seemed like a crazy idea into a profitable business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S4 for the compliment and recognition of his hard work.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 challenges the necessity of an investment, stating the business is not large enough to require a partner.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends the business value by mentioning their pending utility patent for the sealed cavity around the crown.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if there are many other banana preservation devices currently on the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that there are none and they will be the first of their kind.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 jokingly asks if there is a banana preservation society they could join.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 plays along with the joke, suggesting they could join the society together.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, reiterating his belief that the founder does not need a partner for this business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if the founder is still working his full-time job.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that he is still employed full-time.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks who is responsible for running the day-to-day operations of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that he is the sole employee and runs the business entirely by himself.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if the founder owns one hundred percent of the equity in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms he owns it entirely, noting that his wife helps and they recently had a baby.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses belief that the product could become wildly successful and shows interest in investing.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 states he will only offer half the requested money and requires another investor to join him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 expresses interest in providing the other half of the money to partner with S3.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokes about the potential for a global banana brand with the two investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks S3 and S1 what percentage of equity they are seeking for their potential joint investment.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 makes an offer of seventy-five thousand dollars for fifteen percent equity, requiring another investor.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 joins S3's offer, stating she would take fifteen percent for the other seventy-five thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 hesitates, noting that there is still another investor who has not made an offer yet.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 urges F1 to consider the value of having two experienced investors with national and international reach.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 comments that giving up thirty percent equity is very aggressive and hints at making his own offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states he would be willing to make a deal for ten percent equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 offers one hundred fifty thousand dollars for ten percent equity plus a one dollar per unit royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 notes that S5's offer is more appealing regarding equity compared to the thirty percent asked by the others.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 suggests partnering with S3 instead, jokingly proposing to exclude S1 from the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 jokes that S3, being a Commander of the British Empire, would never betray a woman.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 confirms he is too much of a gentleman to exclude S1 and urges F1 to take their joint offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 tells S3 and S1 that they are asking for too much equity in their joint offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 suggests that F1 should ask S5 how he plans to actively support and grow the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S3 and S1's joint offer, proposing fifteen percent equity for the full one hundred fifty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks S3 if he would be willing to adjust their joint offer to twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 preemptively states he would be willing to close the deal for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 revises the joint offer with S3 to one hundred fifty thousand dollars for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts S1 and S3's revised joint offer of one hundred fifty thousand dollars for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: UNKNOWN
turns.summary: The panel and the founder celebrate the successful deal with hugs and positive remarks.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 jokingly throws a banana peel at S5 and calls him evil after securing the deal over him.
